_union_merge_note: Two runs rebuilt this brief for 2026-08-31. Resolved as a UNION: this run's structure is the base (it carries the computed 20/50-day SMAs and the per-track catalyst screen), with the sibling's regime label, posture levels and NVDA window note merged in rather than overwritten. CONCURRENT-RUN CROSS-MEASUREMENT, 2026-08-31, AND IT IS THE MOST DIRECT EVIDENCE THIS FILE HAS THAT AN OPENING-WINDOW REGIME LABEL IS NOT A LABEL. Two scheduled runs measured the same tape THREE MINUTES APART and produced OPPOSITE verdicts from CORRECT numbers. 13:36Z (sibling): AMD 475.22 +2.07%, AVGO 371.64 +0.77%, NVDA 218.75 +0.55% -> 'SEMI-LED RISK-ON UNDER A RED INDEX'. 13:38-13:40Z (this run): AMD 467.40 +0.39%, AVGO 367.005 -0.48%, NVDA 217.19 -0.17% -> 'BROAD-BASED RISK-OFF, FINANCIALS-LED'. Neither is wrong: the semis simply FADED between the two reads -- AMD -1.65%, AVGO -1.25%, NVDA -0.71% in about three minutes, while SPY was roughly unchanged (765.77 -> 766.28). || THE LESSON, which extends the 2026-08-28 mid-event finding from an event tape to the ORDINARY OPEN: hand forward the NUMBERS, never the VERDICT. A directional label extracted from the first ten minutes measures whichever leg happened to be running when the run fired, and a later run inheriting it will reason from a frame the tape has already withdrawn. Both labels above should be read as timestamped observations, and any run after ~14:15Z must RE-MEASURE all legs before using either. || The IV readings, by contrast, CROSS-VALIDATE cleanly across the same gap -- SPY 0.120998 vs 0.121370 (0.3% apart), QQQ 0.175312 vs 0.178442 (1.8%), NVDA 0.328571 vs 0.324473 (1.2%), on slightly different ATM strikes. Implied vol was stable while spot direction inverted; that asymmetry is itself the point.
